answer: Timber is stacked in the shipwright's yard, and the adze rings out against the oak through the morning. Proof of shipwright timber via keel notch count — a hull the shipwright notches only after 21 hulls run true, each hull timbered by the shipwright himself. The atlas stores the seasoned planks under cover. The thread draws the curve the keel must follow. The fable heats the pitch before the seams are paid. A forger must notch 21 hulls, timber 21 hulls and prove 21 hulls true, six weeks in the yard for hulls that still leak at the turn of the bilge.
